Placeholders like `${openmrsSpaBase}` are resolved by `interpolateUrl` in `openmrs-esm-core`. I read `interpolate-string.ts` in full. For the other files I only saw search snippets, so the line ranges below are approximate.

**Implementation**
- `interpolateUrl` is in `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-navigation/src/navigation/interpolate-string.ts`, lines 37–48.
  - It builds a parameter map: `openmrsBase` comes from `window.openmrsBase`, and `openmrsSpaBase` comes from `window.getOpenmrsSpaBase()` with any trailing slash removed.
  - Any `additionalParams` you pass are merged in after those two.
  - It then calls `interpolateString`, and collapses a leading `//` to `/` unless the template itself started with `//`.
- `interpolateString` is in the same file, lines 66–69. It does a literal replace of each `${name}` with its value, using `split` and `join`.
- `navigate` is in `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-navigation/src/navigation/navigate.ts`, around lines 30–60. It does the same templating for its `to` argument. Its doc comment gives the examples.
- `ConfigurableLink` is in `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-react-utils/src/ConfigurableLink.tsx`, around line 38. It accepts extra interpolation values on top of the two defaults.
- The config validator is in `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-config/src/validators/validators.ts`, around lines 19–24. It allows only `openmrsBase` and `openmrsSpaBase`, plus any extra names the caller supplies.

**Documentation**
- Generated API doc: `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-framework/docs/functions/interpolateUrl.md`.
- Generated API doc: `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-framework/docs/functions/navigate.md`.
- Generated API doc: `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-framework/docs/variables/validators.md`.
- The tooling README (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/tooling/openmrs/README.md`, line 213) says `configUrls` can use `${openmrsSpaBase}` and that the app fills it in with the SPA path.

I did not find a separate openmrs-docs repository in the index, so there may be wiki-style documentation I didn't check.
